configurePresets.name: base
configurePresets.description: Layout shared by every preset. binaryDir is a sibling of the repo so the source tree stays clean, and ${presetName} gives each configuration its own directory so switching between them does not thrash one CMake cache.

configurePresets.name: release
configurePresets.description: What a contributor builds by default. -Werror stays off: a compiler upgrade can add a warning at any time and a fresh clone should still build.

configurePresets.name: cli-only
configurePresets.description: For a headless machine that will only ever run qsv2flv-cli. The counterpart to QSV2FLV_WITH_GUI=0 in the install scripts, and the answer to a `Could NOT find Qt6` that is not worth fixing.

configurePresets.name: asan-ubsan
configurePresets.description: No Qt: nothing the sanitizers care about is in the GUI, and skipping it keeps QApplication's static registries out of the report. ASan and UBSan share a binary safely; TSan would not, and would need a preset of its own.

configurePresets.name: ci-release
configurePresets.description: release plus -Werror. A separate preset rather than -DQSV2FLV_WERROR=ON in the workflow, so no build setting lives in YAML and `cmake --list-presets` enumerates every configuration this project has.

configurePresets.name: ci-asan-ubsan
configurePresets.description: asan-ubsan plus -Werror. The sanitizer build compiles the same sources at a different optimisation level, where the compiler's uninitialised-use analysis reaches different conclusions.

testPresets.name: base
testPresets.description: --output-on-failure always: the suites print the file, line and both sides of every failed comparison, and none of that is worth anything if CTest swallows it behind "Failed". noTestsAction=error catches a configuration that silently built no tests, which otherwise reads as a pass -- CTest's own default is to shrug and exit 0.
